## Historical audit — S0347

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v3/results/H04/development/commons_105241439/1/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to JSONL lines in this file. All observations were supplied as complete line ranges; no observations were split.

| Evidence | Observed operations and results |
|---|---|
| Goal — line 1, `model_request` | Reconstruct one indoor RGB image as separate editable SceneAct/Blender meshes, matching viewpoint, framing, appearance and occlusions. The student’s inventory interprets it as a classroom; that interpretation is not independent verification of the unseen reference. |
| Initial build — lines 3–4, H `model_response` and step 1 `execute` | Code creates architecture, a two-panel chalkboard, hanging notice, three desks and three chairs. Named children include tops, legs, seats, backs and supports; grouping and coordinates are evidence of intended connections, not proof that connections visually or geometrically match. Colors and geometric chalk marks approximate surfaces. Camera, world and two area lights are configured. No person or articulated pose is represented. |
| First validation — lines 6, 8–11 | Build and render completed; step 1 was selected and the rendered image and reference were supplied to H. The projection table puts the foreground left landmark at `(-.052, 1.038)` against estimated `(.09, .89)`, while board landmarks are closer. These are projections of chosen points, not contour or visibility verification. |
| Revision — lines 13–14, 16–21 | H reported that the first render cropped foreground desks and made the board pale with raised-looking marks. It kept the camera fixed, raised/repositioned furniture, raised the blue boundary and replaced much chalk geometry with procedural board materials. Step 2 built and rendered successfully. H’s subsequent comparison is evidence of its assessment, not an independent image check. |
| Final revision and result — lines 23–24, 26, 28–30 | H reported that step 2 remained pale and striped and that foreground crops differed. It darkened and altered board shading, narrowed the board, adjusted desks and raised the floor/baseboard, retaining camera and lights. Step 3 built and rendered successfully and was selected. Its projected board corners nearly match the estimates, but the foreground landmark is `(.096, .942)` versus `(.09, .89)`. No subsequent visual review or `DONE` is recorded. |

**Input and exploration.** The actual instructional input included inventory, complexity and projection-check requirements, followed by requests to compare each available render with the reference (lines 1, 11, 21). No separate teacher detection, diagnosis, proposed patch, or teacher-to-student feedback appears in this trace; adoption of such feedback is therefore not established. H independently chose and executed two revisions in response to render feedback. Sessions report no student tool calls beyond the runner-mediated executions (lines 2, 12, 22).

**Outcome and uncertainty.** This is a **formal execution/render success**, not established reconstruction success: all three executions returned `ok`, and the last was selected, but neither reference nor rendered pixels are visible in this audit. The final appearance, actual object completeness, part connections, furniture placement and camera/light fidelity remain unverified. H’s second-render diagnosis and its hypothesis that darker, broader procedural wiping would improve the board were not checked in a recorded final comparison.

**Lessons.** Transferably, comparing foreground and background landmarks can distinguish a local adjustment hypothesis from a global camera change, but projections cannot validate appearance or occlusion. Task-specific choices here were classroom furniture repositioning and chalkboard shading; their effectiveness remains uncertain.
